introduction: On this Sunday, Elisha feeds a hundred people with twenty barley loaves, and there is some left over. In the Gospel, Jesus takes a boy's five barley loaves and two fish and feeds a crowd of five thousand. For the next few Sundays we will hear from Saint John's Gospel about Jesus, the bread of life. Paul urges us to keep the unity of the Spirit. Let us bring the little we have to the Lord.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the eyes of all look to the Lord, and he gives them food in due season. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be one body and one Spirit, with one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the hungry of the world: that the generosity of many may feed them, and that no food may be wasted. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who feel they have too little to offer: that they may bring what they have to Christ, like the boy with the loaves. Let us pray to the Lord.
For farmers, bakers and all who provide our food: that their work may be blessed and fairly rewarded. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may receive the Eucharist with gratitude and share our bread with others. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you open your hand and satisfy every living thing. Bless what we bring you, multiply it for the good of others, and feed us with the bread of life. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Five barley loaves and two fish
reflection.body:
In the first reading, a man brings the prophet Elisha twenty barley loaves, a gift of first fruits. Elisha says, "Give to the people, that they may eat." His servant protests that it will not go far among a hundred people. But it is enough, and there is some left over, "according to the LORD's word."

The Gospel tells of a far greater feeding. A huge crowd follows Jesus. He asks Philip, "Where are we to buy bread, that these may eat?" Philip does the arithmetic: "Two hundred denarii worth of bread is not sufficient for them." Andrew finds a boy with food, but wonders, "There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these among so many?"

Jesus has the people sit down. He takes the loaves, gives thanks and distributes them, and everyone eats as much as they want. Then he says, "Gather up the broken pieces which are left over, that nothing be lost." They fill twelve baskets.

John does not call this a miracle but a sign. It points beyond itself. Over the next Sundays, Jesus will explain it: he himself is the bread of life, given in the Eucharist. The words "took the loaves, and having given thanks" already sound like the Mass.

The story also says something about us. The miracle began with a boy who gave what he had, small as it was. Jesus did not create bread from nothing; he took what was offered. And nothing was to be wasted.

This week, bring to Jesus the little you have: a little time, a little money, a little faith. Offer it with thanks, and see what he does with it. And think about food you waste, and how you might share more with those who are hungry.
